items.stem: Why is a scaffold split often preferred over a random split when evaluating a molecular-property model?

options.text: It reduces leakage of near-identical molecules between train and test
options.rationale: Correct: scaffold splits test generalisation to novel chemistry.

options.text: It guarantees a higher test score
options.rationale: It usually lowers, and more honestly estimates, performance.

options.text: It removes the need for a test set
options.rationale: A separate test set is still required.
Splitting does not add any data.

items.explanation: Correct: scaffold splits test generalisation to novel chemistry.

options.rationale: Correct: graphs capture connectivity for graph models.
One scalar discards most structural information.

options.rationale: Correct: computational predictions require wet-lab validation.

options.text: The compound is proven to be an effective drug
options.rationale: No efficacy is established in silico.

options.text: The output is a clinical recommendation
options.rationale: It is not medical advice or a clinical claim.
